1.explanation:
• perf-x-report-generator.js is where we assemble and append our synthetic ‘R’-phase events into the trace. If those events are malformed or mis-categorized here, downstream code will render them incorrectly.  
• trace_event_importer.js is responsible for ingesting raw trace events (including phase 'R') and mapping them into timeline model events. A bug here can cause mark events to be treated like duration slices.  
• x_marker_annotation.js defines the model for an instant (X-marker) annotation. If the importer isn’t tagging events with this annotation type, or if the model itself has incorrect defaults, the UI will draw them as slices.  
• x_marker_annotation_view.js is the view layer that draws those instant annotations. A rendering bug here (or improper event dispatch) can result in using the normal slice renderer instead of the thin-line marker renderer.
1.bug_scenario: When you run Lighthouse with “--save-assets” (or use the injectMetrics.js script) you append synthetic Lighthouse metrics (First Contentful Paint, First Meaningful Paint, etc.) into a Chrome trace as phase “R” mark events. In DevTools > Timeline (or chrome://tracing) you expect to see thin vertical “marker” lines at the exact timestamps. Instead, you get long colored slices under the “Interactions” lane — the synthetic marks are being rendered as full-duration slices rather than instant markers.

2.explanation:
• lighthouse-cli/performance-experiment/report/perf-x-report-generator.js is where we build and append our synthetic metric events. It currently tags those events with phase “R”, which isn’t being treated as an instantaneous marker by the viewer, so they render as zero-duration slices with minimum width rather than slender vertical markers.  
• lighthouse-core/closure/third_party/DevtoolsTimelineModel.js (the upstream DevTools model copy) parses incoming trace events and decides how to classify “mark” events. It must be updated or configured to recognize our Lighthouse category/phase pairing and expose them as markers instead of generic slices.  
• lighthouse-core/third_party/traceviewer-js/importer/trace_event_importer.js transforms raw trace JSON into model events. Right now it doesn’t map phase “R” events in category “lighthouse” into its InstantEvent type, so downstream code treats them like complete slices.  
• lighthouse-core/third_party/traceviewer-js/model/x_marker_annotation.js defines the data model for point-in-time “X-marker” annotations. If our synthetic events aren’t flagged as X-marker events here, the view will never draw them correctly.  
• lighthouse-core/third_party/traceviewer-js/ui/annotations/x_marker_annotation_view.js takes X-marker model entries and paints the little triangles/lines on the timeline. It’ll need no-duration/in-time-only events (not slices) in order to render the thin markers rather than the fat bars you’re seeing.
2.bug_scenario: After injecting synthetic Lighthouse metric events into a DevTools/Lighthouse trace (using phase “R” mark events), opening the resulting trace in chrome://tracing or the DevTools Timeline tab shows thick colored bars under the “Interactions” lane instead of thin, zero-duration vertical markers at the exact timestamps of each metric. In the screenshot you can see long slices spanning hundreds of milliseconds rather than the little triangles or lines expected for point-in-time markers (First Contentful Paint, First Meaningful Paint, etc.).
